newsitem.title: JAPAN: China road transport fuel needs seen surging - study.
newsitem.headline: China road transport fuel needs seen surging - study.

text.p: Increased use of automobiles is expected to boost China's demand for gasoline and gas oil to 2.1 million barrels per day (bpd) by 2010, 3.1 times what the country consumed in 1994, a study showed on Wednesday.

From 1994 to 2010, China's gasoline and gas oil demand is expected to grow by about 1.4 million bpd, which is about the equivalent of Japan's consumption in 1994, the Institute of Energy Economics (IEE), a private think-tank, said.

"China is expected to become a major consumer of oil products such as gasoline and gas oil, as the country becomes more reliant on cars and trucks," Yasuhiro Tanaka, an economist with the IEE, told reporters.
"Existing means of transportation, such as trains and ships, are not expected to have the capacity to accommodate the country's growing economy," Tanaka said.
The number of automobiles in China is forecast to grow from 10.4 million in 1995 to 18 million in 2000 and 40 million in 2010, Tanaka said.
The figures show China will have about 30 automobiles per 1,000 people in 2010, which is about the same as the current situation in the Philippines and Indonesia, he said.
"China will still be at the earliest stage of motorisation in 2010," Tanaka said.
In 2010, China's gasoline demand for automobiles is forecast to be 2.7 times that of 1994, while demand for gas oil is expected to be 4.8 times higher compared to 1994, he said.
Tanaka attributed the sharp jump in gas oil to an increase in the number of trucks using diesel fuel rather than gasoline.
China's crude oil imports are expected to increase sharply after 2000, intensifying competition with Japan for Middle Eastern crudes, Tanaka said.
